reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of the Risk-Constrained Kelly (RCK) framework lies in replacing the unconstrained Kelly maximization of expected log-growth with a constrained version that guarantees a maximum drawdown probability. This is achieved by bounding the moment generating function E[(r'b)^{-λ}] ≤ 1, which implies a tail bound on minimum wealth P(W_min < α) < β via a martingale argument. The constraint is convex in the bet vector b, ensuring tractability. The parameter λ serves as a tuning knob between growth and drawdown risk, with higher λ corresponding to stricter drawdown controls. The QRCK variant approximates the log utility with a quadratic form, yielding a Markowitz-style mean-variance problem with λ acting as a risk aversion coefficient. This allows for efficient numerical solution while preserving the essential structure of risk-sensitive optimization. The framework enables GSE to dynamically adjust bet sizes based on risk tolerance, providing a principled way to avoid catastrophic drawdowns without sacrificing too much expected growth.
